$comment: Generated by `fathom_core::events::schema::to_text()`, blessed by `FATHOM_BLESS=1 cargo test -p fathom-core --test events`. Do not hand-edit: change the types or this generator and bless again. Owner: `e6.7` (`reco-raw`).
description: One thing that happened in one fathom run, as one JSON object on one line of a `.jsonl` file. Written by `fathom why`/`fathom analyze` when the stream is switched on, read back by `fathom events`. A file is a sequence of these lines and nothing else; a line whose `schema_version` this reader cannot read is skipped by name, a field it has not heard of is skipped, and a kind it has not heard of survives as an undeclared kind, because the file outlives the build that wrote it.

contract.description: Which stream this line belongs to. A line whose contract is not this is not a malformed event; it is the wrong file.

counts.description: The numbers, named (`findings`, `hidden`, `suppressed`, `code`, `files`, `added`, `deleted`, `gaps`, …). Names are stable within a major and a name a reader has not seen is a number to ignore; this is where a new measurement arrives without breaking anybody.

detector.description: The detector or plugin finding type the event is about. For a plugin's finding this is the namespaced `plugin.type`, which is what makes a plugin's findings routable.

episode.description: The episode the event is about, when there is one.

kind.description: What happened, spelled `family.fact` — `run`, `analysis`, `detector`, `finding`, `notice`, `gate`, `export`, `watch`. The list below is what this build declares; a kind outside it is an undeclared kind, kept and printed, never a failure.

note.description: The sentence: a notice, a refusal's reason, a finding's message. Free text, and redacted by the writer before the line leaves the process — the schema is not the privacy boundary and does not claim to be.

outcome.description: What the thing did: `ran`, `disabled`, `not_examined`, `suppressed`, `ok`, `error`. `disabled` and `not_examined` are outcomes with the same shape as `ran` so "did it look?" has one answer.

producer.description: What wrote the line, version included, so a stream that spans an upgrade says so in the stream.

repository.description: The repository as a label — a name, never an absolute path.

run.description: One id per verb invocation, e.g. `why-1792855784071`. Two runs writing one stream are pulled apart by this and not by a clock they may not agree on.

schema_version.description: The version of this shape the writer wrote. Additive changes keep it; a reader that cannot read the number says so by name and moves on (which is the whole benefit of the number).

seq.description: This event's position in its run, stamped by the bus and never by the producer, so a stream can be read in order even when two writers share it.

severity.description: As the finding model spells it: `high`, `medium`, `low`.

subject.description: The subject inside the episode — a path, a symbol, a queue id.

ts.description: Wall-clock microseconds since the epoch, supplied by the caller — the domain crate has no clock (ADR-002 §4.1). A reader must not assume it is present.

title: fathom analysis event — one line of the stream

cap.note: a producer refuses more than this many subscribers and counts the refusal rather than slowing every publish down to grow a list

x-fathom.capability: fathom why|analyze --events, read back by `fathom events`
x-fathom.compatibility: additive within a version; an unreadable version is a line a reader skips by name, which is what lets a newer build write for an older reader
consumer: the out-of-tree example plugin's contract test
x-fathom.transport: one object per line (`.jsonl`); this schema describes a line, not the file
x-fathom.unknown_kinds: an undeclared kind is kept with its name rather than refused, because the file outlives the build that wrote it
